Figure 1: Few-shot methods under realistic imbalance and effectiveness of prototype rectification. (Left) Variation of mean Top-1 accuracy across 10 datasets with the number of shots under severe imbalance. Contrary to standard few-shot assumptions, increasing the number of support samples does not necessarily improve performance; instead, several strong baselines degrade as additional samples amplify majority-class bias in prototype estimation. (Right) Performance at 16-shot under near balanced and severe imbalance settings. Our proposed prototype rectification (PRiSM) consistently improves all baselines, with particularly large gains under severe imbalance.

Figure 3: Effect of the Dirichlet concentration parameter δ on class imbalance across three different classes. Smaller δ values yield more skewed class distributions, while larger values approach uniform sampling.
Figure 2: Prototype-block performance as a function of different values of the learning rates. The dotted vertical lines show the Lipschitz-based learning rate.
